Re: Petition for Public Records Order - Oregon State Penitentiary Records
Dear Mr. Haliburton:
This letter is the Attorney General's order on your petition for disclosure of records
under the Oregon Public Records Law, ORS 192.410 to 192.505. Your petition, which we
received on May 10, 1996, asks the Attorney General to direct the Oregon State Penitentiary
(OSP) to make available to you for inspection or produce copies of the following records:
1. Offenders Psychological Report;
2. PSI Report.
For the reasons that follow, we respectfully deny your petition.
The Public Records Law confers a right to access any public record of a public body
in Oregon, subject to certain exemptions and limitations. See ORS 192.420. The law
requires generally that the custodian of public records furnish proper and reasonable
opportunities for inspection and/or copying of the record in the office of the custodian.
ORS 192.430. Any person denied the right to inspect or to receive a copy of any public
record of a state agency may petition the Attorney General to review the public record to
determine if it may be withheld from public inspection. ORS 192.450(1).
ORS 192.430 authorizes state agencies to adopt reasonable rules and regulations
necessary for protecting the records and preventing interference with the regular discharge of
duties of the custodian. ORS 192.430. Moreover, the Public Records Law permits public
bodies to establish and recover fees reasonably calculated to reimburse them for their actual

cost in making public records available, including the time spent by agency staff in locating
and reviewing the requested records in order to delete exempt material. See ORS
192.440(3). See also, Public Records Order, April 7, 1989 (Martin).
Your petition states that you asked to inspect and/ or copy the public records listed in
your petition above on April 21, 1996, but that your request was denied by the OSP Records
Department.
In reviewing your petition with Tamara Blair, Support Services Manager at OSP,
Ms. Blair advises that neither OSP, nor the Oregon Department of Corrections (ODOC),
maintains or possesses a presentence investigation report (PSI) among their records pertaining
to you. Ms. Blair advises further that she has caused a memorandum to be sent to you in
response to your petition reflecting this fact. We understand from Ms. Blair that her
memorandum also advises that OSP will make available to you, upon prepayment of its costs
in accordance with ODOC's fee schedule,11 a copy of the only document in its possession
that appears to fall within the scope of your request and petition -- a three page document
entitled "Offender Profile Report."
Because ODOC does not maintain or possess a PSI report pertaining to you, ODOC
cannot make that report available, and the Attorney General has no authority to order its
disclosure. See ORS 192.450(1). Because ODOC is willing to furnish you with a copy of
its Offender Profile Report concerning you, we deny your petition as moot with respect to
this document.
Sincerely,
ELIZABETH S. HARCHENKO
Special Counsel to the Attorney General
